metric_target: Raw current-action NOUL q, not smoothed alarm R against action labels.
interpretation: Asymmetric EMA training improves raw AP over the matched NOUL control in both evaluated domains in this seed, and is the numerically best external arm. Raw-up is stronger on synthetic classification and unsafe-pair growth but transfers worse externally. Asymmetric EMA does not reduce synthetic raw false alarms. No general or seed-robust superiority is established.
memory_scope: Fast rises and bounded slow decay are properties of the recurrence. 107/128 increasing unsafe pairs across safe gaps are ordered correctly by asymmetric alarm R, not all pairs. There is no independent active-threat-state gold and no claim of state accuracy or calibrated harm probability.
limitations: One fixed seed; no training-seed robustness or statistical significance claim.
Both test sets were previously inspected; exploratory comparison.
The new raw-up control shares full chronological trajectory updates and extended verified unsafe pairs with both EMA arms. Earlier trained controls are not directly matched.
No automatic alpha/lambda search, additional seeds or new training runs are assigned.
